items.briefing:
Google has warned that AI is actively changing how cyber attacks are carried out, making threats faster and harder to detect — a concern for all Australian organisations. This follows a real-world incident where an AI agent breached a Spanish organisation and modified personal data, showing these risks are no longer theoretical. Separately, a Cisco zero-day vulnerability involving API authentication has been disclosed, and organisations using Cisco products should check with their IT teams about applying any available patches promptly.

On a positive note, Australia's involvement in global anti-scam alliances continues to grow, with the Global Signal Exchange joining Japan's anti-scam efforts — strengthening protections for Australians targeted by international scams. **Practical tip:** If your organisation uses AI tools like ChatGPT for work tasks, avoid pasting in confidential or client information — follow the lead of banks now actively blocking such data leaks.

featured.title: Cisco Zero-Day Highlights API Endpoint Authentication Issues
featured.summary: The authentication bypass flaw CVE-2026-76460 impacts Cisco's Identity Services Engine (ISE) and received a maximum 10 out of 10 CVSS score.
